outline:
本課程提供學生及職前專業人士必備之英語文語言技巧，強調工程專業領域之英文溝通能力之訓練。課程內容依學院專業內容區分並整合英語文之聽說讀寫之能力為未來全球化移動及以英語專業溝通人才培育為目標。
This course aims to provide pre-service engineering students/professionals with the adequate skills of the English language and communicative competence to facilitate their current academic and future career pursuits. Students are encouraged to utilize their domain expertise to participate in professional communication in English. Centered on the training of professional use of the English language, the ESP curriculum as the crux of a highly-integrated work of domain knowledge and the English learning development embodies the indispensable credentials required for a global profession.
schedule:
Main course sequence: Engineering Units 1–3 before the midterm; selected Units 4–9 in Weeks 10–15, with review and guided practice. 北科之英 coverage is limited to Unit 1. Selected BESTEP activities support speaking, writing and visual-information skills.

Week 1 (07 Sep–13 Sep 2026): Orientation, diagnostic tasks and learning resources.

Week 2 (14 Sep–20 Sep 2026): Engineering and 北科之英 Unit 1: introductory reading, vocabulary and short writing.

Week 3 (21 Sep–27 Sep 2026): BESTEP speaking and professional reading practice.

Week 4 (28 Sep–04 Oct 2026): Chart and data language; speaking practice.

Week 5 (05 Oct–11 Oct 2026): Drawing and design language; consolidation.

Week 6 (12 Oct–18 Oct 2026): Essay structure, thesis, paragraph development and short recommendation writing.

Week 7 (19 Oct–25 Oct 2026): 21 October: Jack the Ripper portrait and family-background discussion; 22 October: design an environmental solution.

Week 8 (26 Oct–01 Nov 2026): Engineering Unit 3: over-design and factors of safety; inquiry-email writing and TOEIC Unit 4 practice.

Week 9 (2–8 November 2026): Midterm examination week; university common English examination on 3 November. No separate course midterm essay.

Week 10 (11 and 12 November 2026): Engineering Unit 4: Horizontal and vertical measurements, selected pp. 14–15.
Activity: Guided reading, vocabulary and a short spoken or written response.

Week 11 (18 and 19 November 2026): Engineering Unit 5: Locating and setting out, selected pp. 16–17.
Activity: Technical-process explanation and questions; selected BESTEP listening/reading practice.

Week 12 (25 and 26 November 2026): Engineering Unit 6: Dimensions of circles, selected pp. 18–19.
Activity: Reading discussion and technical-report preparation; selected BESTEP visual-information practice.

Week 13 (2 and 3 December 2026): Engineering Unit 7: Dimensional accuracy, selected pp. 20–21.
Activity: Handwritten technical report (150–200 words): describe a failure, identify its cause and recommend a fix; peer review.

Week 14 (9 and 10 December 2026): Engineering Unit 8: Numbers and calculations, selected pp. 22–23.
Activity: Technical-report revision after feedback; prepare the final video, outline and script.

Week 15 (16 and 17 December 2026): Engineering Unit 9: Area, size and mass, selected pp. 24–25.
Activity: Group video (5–8 minutes), visual-aid explanation and questions; finalize the outline and script.

Week 16 (21–27 December 2026): Final submission of the video, annotated outline and full script; file-access checks. Submission period only.
scorePolicy:
Percentages of the final semester grade:
Coursework: 36%
speaking tasks: 12%
writing tasks: 12%
Attendance: 12%
Final assessment: 24%
Cool English independent learning, Weeks 17–18: 20%
University common English examination: 20%
Total: 100%.

Speaking (12%): recordings, chart explanations and technical-process tasks. Writing (12%): short writing and the Weeks 13–14 technical report with revision. The final video remains a combined 24% assessment. There is no separate midterm essay.

Skill evidence: at least three assessed speaking outputs and two writing outputs, including revision after feedback, drawn from the scheduled course tasks.
Speaking criteria: Content and Task Fulfillment; Organization and Coherence; Language Use; Delivery and Fluency; Interaction and Response.
Writing criteria: Content and Task Fulfillment; Organization and Coherence; Language Use; Genre and Professional Appropriacy; Revision and Development.
Assessments use the official four-level descriptors. At least one speaking assessment covers all five dimensions; interaction is marked N/A when inapplicable to another task.

Graded tasks within each coursework skill component are averaged equally. A draft and its revision count as one writing task. Midterm and final components are counted separately. Attendance begins at 100: the first three absences have no deduction, then five attendance points are deducted per additional absence. Approved leave follows university rules.

【BESTEP與英語能力認列】

BESTEP Speaking and Writing: 17 October 2026.
BESTEP Listening and Reading: 21 November 2026.
University common English examination: 3 November 2026, 10:10–11:25; separate 20% semester component.

Actual BESTEP participation earns 10 bonus points; an eligible other English proficiency test earns 5. Submit the required evidence by the end of the semester. Each score report is counted once, and the semester grade is capped at 100.

A verified B2 speaking or writing result may satisfy the designated 10 percentage points for that skill. The remaining 2 points in a 12-point allocation, or 6 in a 16-point allocation, are assessed through course work. Students continue to participate in the learning activities and complete the other requirements.
materials:
Main textbook: Mark Ibbotson, Professional English in Use: Engineering, Cambridge University Press, 2009. Units 1–3 before the midterm; selected Units 4–9, pp. 14–25, for Weeks 10–15.
Supplementary reading already used: 北科之英 (Taipei Tech ESP Chemical Engineering), National Taipei University of Technology Language Center, Unit 1: The Scientific Method.
BESTEP materials: EAP Power Up: Synthesizing Textual and Visual Information for Academic Success, Language Training & Testing Center (LTTC), 2024; selected activities in reading, summarising and explaining visual information.
Additional materials: instructor-prepared slides, task sheets and assessment rubrics; cited news/data sources; Cool English online exercises.
remarks: 本課程為專業英文（ESP/EAP）課程，教材、講義及簡報均採全英文；課堂授課及師生互動之英語使用比例90% (含)以上。
resources:
● 混成學習 (Blended Learning)
課程結合實體授課與線上學習（同步視訊／非同步活動）。
Combines face-to-face instruction with online learning (including synchronous video sessions or asynchronous activities).
● 參與式創新教學 (Participatory & Innovative Teaching)
強調學生參與與產出，導入翻轉、PBL/專題、設計思考或遊戲化等策略。
Emphasizes student engagement and outcomes by adopting strategies such as Flipped Classroom, PBL (Problem/Project- Based Learning), Design Thinking, or Gamification.
● 數位教材資源應用 (Application of Digital Resources)
採用影音多媒體或具開放授權之資源（如OCW、開放教科書）作為主要或輔助教材。
Adopts multimedia or open-licensed resources (e.g., OCW, Open Textbooks) as primary or supplementary teaching materials.
● 數位科技融入 (Digital Technology Integration)
運用生成式AI、VR/AR、IoT、IRS等新興科技輔助教學與評量。
Utilizes emerging technologies such as Generative AI, VR/AR, IoT, and IRS (Interactive Response Systems) to facilitate teaching and assessment.
